correctness.rationale: The claim fixes the 14-vertex Fano incidence Heawood graph with (p_i,l_j) edges iff (i-j) mod 7 in {0,1,3}, unit geometric edges, vertex-centered closed balls of radius r/2, and inclusive thresholds. Adams–Shukla–Singh Lemma 2.2 rigorously reduces every real r>=0 to integer-threshold subface-generated complexes. At r=0 there are 14 components; r=1 is a connected 14-vertex/21-edge incidence graph of cycle rank 8. At r=2 independent code generated 147 simplices (f=(14,63,56,14)) and replayed all 56 elementary free-face collapses: 14 (neighbor-triangle,tetrahedron) plus 42 (distance-two edge,triangle), retaining exactly the original graph, hence the degree-one class persists. At r=3 independent code reconstructed all 847 nonempty faces (f=(14,91,308,287,126,21)) and the specified toggle matching; exactly 399 pairs, one critical vertex and 48 critical 2-simplices, and an independently constructed 3010-incidence oriented Hasse graph was topologically sorted in full with no cycle. Forman discrete Morse therefore gives one 0-cell and 48 two-cells, hence wedge of 48 S^2, not merely mod-two homology. At r=4 the independent enumeration gave 7919 nonempty faces (f=(14,91,364,1001,2002,2219,1472,602,140,14)), 3927 matching pairs with one critical vertex and 64 critical four-simplices, and all 45122 oriented incidences acyclic. Independently, exact enumeration verified the decomposition into two contractible cones A,B with |A∩B|=1295 and equality A∩B=B_P*B_L; each Fano triple complex collapses to a connected 7-vertex 14-edge graph (rank 8), so the suspension-of-join homotopy pushout yields wedge^{64} S^4. At r=5 each closed radius-two edge-endpoint neighborhood union is all 14 vertices, so the nerve is full simplex thereafter. Distinct homology degrees at successive scales and the relative r=1 to r=2 collapse give exactly 13 reduced H_0 [0,1), eight H_1 [1,3), forty-eight H_2 [3,4), sixty-four H_4 [4,5). Homotopy CW models establish free integral groups. Independent calculations were exhaustive for THIS finite graph; the original verify.py code was read, not relied upon as a black-box exit log. No theorem asserted for larger incidence planes.

value.rationale: The Heawood graph is the canonical smallest cubic graph with girth six. Its intrinsic metric Čech persistence at r=3 lies exactly at the first scale where the standard girth-based graph-recovery theorem no longer applies. The previously unclassified new homotopy shift to 48 two-spheres, followed by the quantitatively different 64 four-sphere stage, yields a complete natural integral persistence classification of a fundamental test graph, useful for comparing Rips versus geometric-ball nerves. The earlier general q-family scale-four result limits the novel part but does not make the r=3 calculation a routine textbook consequence. The result is confined to this finite graph and does not imply all projective-plane orders.
